eli: Quick heads-up — ran a kernel-pick sweep on courier (mixed SM86/92 fleet). When the bf16 fastpath is enabled the 1k seq path regresses ~8-12% p50 for batch sizes >8. Strange: small batches are fine.

mika: ugh. did you repro locally or on-canary?

eli: repro on canary only. local dev VM (single sm86) looked OK. suspecting an interaction with continuous batching + kvcache warmup.

jordan: any logs/profile output? can you paste the kernel selection trace?

eli: pasted the short trace below — kernel selector picks bf16-warp-opt for sm86 but then falls back to generic for the matmul in the same op on sm92 nodes (weird ordering).

```
KERNEL_SELECT: model=T5v1.2 seqlen=1024 batch=12
node[0] sm=86 selected=bf16_warp_opt
node[1] sm=92 selected=generic_fp16_fallback
KV_CACHE: hit_ratio ramp 0.12 -> 0.78 during warmup
BATCHER: continuous-batcher threshold=8 triggered
```

perf-bot: bench job 9876 finished — p50 latency +9%, p95 +18% vs baseline. traces attached.

sara: possible causes: wrong sm detection on some nodes (driver string parsing), or kernel constraints failing and triggering fallback mid-op. we saw a driver string with "SMX" in the cuda-toolkit probe last week.

tom: also remember we recently changed the seqlen gating heuristic to prefer wf32/bf16 kernels when kvcache hit >0.5. if the kvcache ramp happens after first few tokens, that could explain small-batch vs large-batch divergence.

mika: idea: add a short-circuit in the selector — require kernel capability check per-device (nvptx compute capability >7.5 and tensor-core fp16/bf16 flags) rather than relying on codepath heuristics. add a fuzz test: mix sm86+sm92 and run multi-node microbench.

eli: agreed. i'll add a hardened capability probe that uses cudaGetDeviceAttribute(CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_COMPUTE_CAPABILITY_MAJOR) and checks for FP16_TENSOR_OPS and BF16 support by trying a tiny cuBLASLt bf16 op. if the op fails, mark device as no-bf16 and skip that kernel.

jordan: can you dump the detection pseudo? saves others time.

eli: pseudo below — will land as a small probe in runtime startup. open to comments.

```
# pseudo
for dev in devices:
  major = cudaGetDeviceAttr(dev, COMPUTE_CAP_MAJOR)
  minor = cudaGetDeviceAttr(dev, COMPUTE_CAP_MINOR)
  has_tc = cudaGetDeviceAttr(dev, TENSOR_OPS) > 0
  bf16_probe_ok = try_small_bf16_gemm(dev)
  device_caps[dev] = {
    "compute": f"{major}.{minor}",
    "tensor_ops": str(has_tc),
    "bf16_ok": str(bf16_probe_ok)
  }
```

sara: sounds good. we should also add telemetry counters when a kernel fallback occurs mid-op (which is currently silent) — that will show how often selector flips.

mika: please add a canary rollout: selector probe off by default, opt-in via runtime flag `--strict-cap-detect` for a week. then flip default if clean.

eli: will implement probe + telemetry + flag. I'll post a short perf run after landing. for immediate mitigation, disabling the bf16 fastpath on the canary pool drops p95 back to baseline.

jordan: thanks. filed a follow-up issue: https://rwd/issue/INF-6142 (notes + traces attached).

perf-bot: alert created INF-6142: kernel-selector/arch-probe regression (severity=medium).

eli: thanks all. I'll update thread when I have a candidate fix. :thumbsup:
